summary: Meta describes how the University of Pittsburgh's HERL lab and ATDev, under an ARPA-H-funded consortium, are integrating Meta's open-source DINO and Segment Anything (SAM) vision models—optimized for edge deployment—into an assistive mobility robotics platform (RAMMP).

mechanisms.reason: The document describes deploying DINOv3 and SAM directly on battery-powered, edge robotic hardware rather than in the datacenter.
mechanisms.quote: Processing camera images and sensor data directly on the device, known as edge computing, empowers robotic mobility platforms to function as responsive tools.

practices.reason: Describes techniques (reduced memory footprint, lower precision, efficient batching) used to run vision models on constrained edge hardware, though tied to this specific project's stack.
practices.quote: engineers optimize models for edge devices, reducing memory footprint, using lower precision when appropriate, and deploying in formats tailored for real-world conditions.
